name: Seychellois Kari Koko (Fish Curry)
description: Kari koko, coconut fish curry, is what most Seychellois point to as their real signature dish - real technique caramelizes the onion first, then blooms real massalé (garam masala) in the oil before the coconut milk and fish go in, building genuine depth rather than just simmering everything together at once.
steps_detailed: Fry the onion in a little oil over medium heat, stirring, 6-7 minutes, until it begins to caramelize.
Stir in the garam masala and cook 2-3 minutes to bloom the spices - this real step builds genuine depth.
Add the ginger, garlic, tomatoes, and jalapeño, and cook 4-5 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add the fish and simmer 8-10 minutes until just cooked through.

name: Seychellois Ladob Banan
description: Ladob banan, ripe plantain simmered in lightly spiced coconut milk, is a beloved Seychellois dessert, real technique using genuinely ripe plantain and real cinnamon and nutmeg together, not nutmeg alone, for its distinctive warm sweetness.
steps_detailed: Simmer the plantain in the coconut milk, sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg, 15-18 minutes, until tender and the sauce has thickened slightly - real technique treats cinnamon as equally essential to nutmeg here, not an afterthought.
Stir in the vanilla off the heat before serving.

description: Ladob fruit à pain, the real savory breadfruit version of ladob, is a genuine Seychellois side dish, made here with real breadfruit, genuinely available frozen through African and Caribbean grocers in the US.
steps_detailed: Simmer the breadfruit in the coconut milk and nutmeg, 20-22 minutes, until tender and the sauce has thickened slightly.

name: Seychellois Satini Papay (Papaya Chutney)
description: Satini papay, a spicy green papaya chutney, is a genuine Seychellois relish, real technique grating the papaya while still green and firm for real crunch.
steps_detailed: Toss the grated papaya with the jalapeño, onion, ginger, and lemon juice.
Let sit at least 15 minutes for the flavors to meld.

name: Seychellois Grilled Fish with Creole Sauce
description: Grilled fish with a real tangy, spicy Creole sauce is a beloved Seychellois staple, often cooked over coconut-husk coals for real distinctive aroma.
steps_detailed: Grill the fish, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.
Meanwhile, cook the onion and garlic 3-4 minutes, then add the tomatoes and jalapeño, and simmer 12-15 minutes into a tangy sauce.
Serve the fish topped with the sauce.

name: Seychellois Coconut Rice
description: Rice cooked in real coconut milk, sometimes with a real pinch of saffron, a common Seychellois accompaniment to curry.
steps_detailed: Soak the saffron in a tablespoon of warm water for 10 minutes.
Cook the rice with the coconut milk in place of some of the water, along with the saffron and its soaking water, per package timing, until tender.

name: Seychellois Chicken Curry
description: Chicken curry, spiced with real turmeric, cumin, and coriander, is a beloved everyday Seychellois dish, real technique building the spice base before the coconut milk goes in.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the turmeric, cumin, and coriander, and cook 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk and simmer 20-22 minutes until the chicken is tender.
